title: Alabama White Sauce Pulled Pork
seoTitle: Alabama White Sauce Pulled Pork | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Northern Alabama white sauce on pulled pork—bright, tangy, holds well
subtitle: Smoked shoulder finished with tangy mayo-vinegar sauce for ten
description: Adapted from classic Alabama white BBQ sauce tradition (Amazing Ribs, Hey Grill Hey): pork shoulder smokes with a simple rub, gets pulled, and tossed with tangy mayo-vinegar white sauce for sandwiches.

steps.title: Season the shoulder
steps.instruction: Coat with mustard binder. Rub with salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic powder. Rest 20 minutes while smoker heats to 250°F.

steps.title: Smoke to 165°F
steps.instruction: Smoke shoulder fat-side up at 250°F until bark is set and internal temp hits 165°F, about 5–6 hours.

steps.title: Make white sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk mayo, vinegar, lemon juice, horseradish, cayenne, and pinch of salt. Chill until service.

steps.title: Wrap to 203°F
steps.instruction: Wrap in foil. Continue at 250°F until probe-tender and 203°F internal, about 2–3 hours.

steps.title: Rest, pull, and sauce
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 40 minutes. Pull pork into a pan. Toss with white sauce to coat—start with 1 cup and add to taste.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Cover sauced pork with foil and hold at 170°F. Keep extra white sauce cold on ice for finishing.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: White-sauce pulled pork, buns, chopped pickles, extra sauce. Alabama-style sandwiches.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered at 325°F. Refresh with cold white sauce after reheating so it stays tangy.

proTips: Toss with sauce after pulling—never mop raw shoulder with serving sauce.
Horseradish is the secret bite; don't skip it.
Chopped pickles on the sandwich add crunch that white sauce loves.
tonightSpread: Sauced pulled pork in a hotel pan.
Buns, pickles, and extra white sauce on ice.
leftovers: Mix into potato salad for a tangy second-day lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: White sauce cuts through rich pork and stays creamy on the hold line. Different from red BBQ without being weird—crews love the tang.
mealPrepNotes: Make white sauce early and chill. Pull pork and toss with sauce just before service, or hold sauced pork covered at 170°F up to 90 minutes.
